name: DREO Solaris Slim H3
summary: A 16 in ceramic heater that stands on a 5.9 in circle, small enough for a desk corner or a narrow gap by the bed. Three hands-on reviews back it, including two winters in a Brooklyn apartment, but CNN Underscored found it weaker on a desk than the bigger 718 and measured 47 dB at its loudest.
idealFor: Studios where floor space is the tightest constraint
Heating one person at a desk or by the bed
pros: Digital thermostat in 1°F steps, 70° oscillation, remote and 12-hour timer
Used for two winters in a Brooklyn one-bedroom (Apartment Therapy)
cons: 47 dB at its loudest in CNN Underscored's test, louder than the 718
CNN found it weaker than the 718 when heating a desk area
Controls are less intuitive than on other models (Bob Vila)
1-year warranty, and DREO recalled a different heater on Oct 29, 2026

trust.summary: Three independent reviews with real use, though CNN Underscored was less impressed than the other two. DREO publishes dimensions, weight and measurable claims, and Bob Vila's noise figure matches the spec. It loses points for DREO's October 2026 recall of another heater, an unverified UL or ETL listing, no declared materials or warnings on the page and a 1-year warranty.

sources.title: Bob Vila: The best electric heaters, tested
sources.note: Best overall, Oct 4, 2026. Michelle Larson used it at her desk; warmed spaces well beyond its 200 sq ft rating; 37.5 dB; reduced humidity least of the 13 heaters over 3 hours; tip-over shutoff; controls less intuitive, no cord storage
